claim: Deregulation of Pol III products causes a range of diseases, including neural diseases and cancers.
source: Deregulation of Pol III products causes a range of diseases, including neural diseases and cancers.
evidence: This is a general statement about the relationship between Pol III products and disease, drawing on established scientific knowledge.

claim: STAT3 positively regulates the activities of Pol III-dependent transcription.
source: Here, we show that STAT3 positively regulates the activities of Pol III-dependent transcription and cancer cell growth.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including RT-qPCR and ChIP assays.

claim: STAT3 positively regulates cancer cell growth.
source: Here, we show that STAT3 positively regulates the activities of Pol III-dependent transcription and cancer cell growth.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell proliferation assays and tumor formation experiments in nude mice.

claim: STAT3 inhibits the expression of TP73, a member of the p53 family.
source: RNA-seq analysis revealed that STAT3 inhibits the expression of TP73, a member of the p53 family.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and validated by RT-qPCR and western blot analyses.

claim: TP73 is required for the regulation of Pol III-directed transcription mediated by STAT3.
source: We found that TP73 is not only required for the regulation of Pol III-directed transcription mediated by STAT3 but also independently suppresses the synthesis of Pol III products.
evidence: This claim is supported by experiments showing that TP73 knockdown reverses the effects of STAT3 silencing on Pol III transcription.

claim: TP73 independently suppresses the synthesis of Pol III products.
source: We found that TP73 is not only required for the regulation of Pol III-directed transcription mediated by STAT3 but also independently suppresses the synthesis of Pol III products.
evidence: This claim is supported by experiments showing that TP73 knockdown alone increases Pol III product levels.

claim: TP73 can disrupt the assembly of TFIIIB subunits by interacting with TFIIIB subunit TBP.
source: Mechanistically, TP73 can disrupt the assembly of TFIIIB subunits and inhibit their occupancies at Pol III target loci by interacting with TFIIIB subunit TBP.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation assays showing interaction between TP73 and TBP, and that TP73 silencing increases TBP-BRF1 interaction.

claim: TP73 inhibits the occupancies of TFIIIB subunits at Pol III target loci.
source: Mechanistically, TP73 can disrupt the assembly of TFIIIB subunits and inhibit their occupancies at Pol III target loci by interacting with TFIIIB subunit TBP.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP assays showing increased occupancy of TFIIIB components at Pol III target loci upon TP73 silencing.

claim: MiR-106a-5p can activate Pol III-directed transcription by targeting the TP73 mRNA 3' UTR to reduce TP73 expression.
source: MiR-106a-5p can activate Pol III-directed transcription by targeting the TP73 mRNA 3' UTR to reduce TP 73 expression.
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase reporter assays and experiments showing that miR-106a-5p mimics reduce TP73 expression and increase Pol III products.

claim: STAT3 activates the expression of miR-106a-5p by binding to the miRNA promoter.
source: We show that STAT3 activates the expression of miR-106a-5p by binding to the miRNA promoter, indicating that the miR-106a-5p links STAT3 with TP73 to regulate Pol III-directed transcription.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP assays showing STAT3 binding to the miR-106a-5p promoter and luciferase assays showing STAT3 regulates promoter activity.

claim: miR-106a-5p links STAT3 with TP73 to regulate Pol III-directed transcription.
source: We show that STAT3 activates the expression of miR-106a-5p by binding to the miRNA promoter, indicating that the miR-106a-5p links STAT3 with TP73 to regulate Pol III-directed transcription.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing STAT3 regulates miR-106a-5p, which in turn regulates TP73, which regulates Pol III transcription.

claim: STAT3 functions as a positive regulator in Pol III-directed transcription by controlling the miR-106a-5p/TP73 axis.
source: Collectively, these findings indicate that STAT3 functions as a positive regulator in Pol III-directed transcription by controlling the miR-106a-5p/TP73 axis.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by the collective experimental data showing the regulatory pathway from STAT3 through miR-106a-5p and TP73 to Pol III transcription.

claim: Human RNA polymerase III consists of 17 subunits.
source: Human RNA polymerase III consisting of 17 subunits synthesizes a subset of medium-sized non-coding RNA molecules, including tRNA, 5S rRNA, 7SL RNA, U6 snRNA, and others.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the composition of RNA polymerase III.

claim: RNA polymerase III synthesizes tRNA, 5S rRNA, 7SL RNA, U6 snRNA, and other medium-sized non-coding RNA molecules.
source: Human RNA polymerase III consisting of 17 subunits synthesizes a subset of medium-sized non-coding RNA molecules, including tRNA, 5S rRNA, 7SL RNA, U6 snRNA, and others.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the products of RNA polymerase III, supported by citations.

claim: 5S rRNA and tRNA are essential to translation.
source: Some of these RNA molecules have been well characterized and are essential to a range of cellular activities such as translation (5S rRNA and tRNA), RNA splicing (U6 snRNA), protein translocation (7SL RNA), Pol II transcription elongation (7SK RNA), and so on Moir and Willis, 2013; Turowski and Tollervey, 2016; Leśniewska and Boguta, 2017; Willis and Moir, 2018; Yeganeh and Hernandez, 2020.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: U6 snRNA is essential to RNA splicing.
source: Some of these RNA molecules have been well characterized and are essential to a range of cellular activities such as translation (5S rRNA and tRNA), RNA splicing (U6 snRNA), protein translocation (7SL RNA), Pol II transcription elongation (7SK RNA), and so on Moir and Willis, 2013; Turowski and Tollervey, 2016; Leśniewska and Boguta, 2017; Willis and Moir, 2018; Yeganeh and Hernandez, 2020.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: 7SL RNA is essential to protein translocation.
source: Some of these RNA molecules have been well characterized and are essential to a range of cellular activities such as translation (5S rRNA and tRNA), RNA splicing (U6 snRNA), protein translocation (7SL RNA), Pol II transcription elongation (7SK RNA), and so on Moir and Willis, 2013; Turowski and Tollervey, 2016; Leśniewska and Boguta, 2017; Willis and Moir, 2018; Yeganeh and Hernandez, 2020.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: 7SK RNA is essential to Pol II transcription elongation.
source: Some of these RNA molecules have been well characterized and are essential to a range of cellular activities such as translation (5S rRNA and tRNA), RNA splicing (U6 snRNA), protein translocation (7SL RNA), Pol II transcription elongation (7SK RNA), and so on Moir and Willis, 2013; Turowski and Tollervey, 2016; Leśniewska and Boguta, 2017; Willis and Moir, 2018; Yeganeh and Hernandez, 2020.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Pol III transcription initiation can be classified into three initiation modes (types I, II, and III).
source: Transcription initiation relies on the occupancy of Pol III apparatus at the promoters of Pol III-transcribed genes and can be classified into three initiation modes (types I, II, and III; Moir and Willis, 2013; Turowski and Tollervey, 2016; Leśniewska and Boguta, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Pol III transcription initiation, supported by citations.

claim: During type II transcription initiation of tRNA genes, TFIIIC initially binds to the internal elements box-A and box-B within the tRNA-coding region.
source: During the transcription initiation of tRNA genes (type II), TFIIIC initially binds to the internal elements box-A and box-B within the tRNA-coding region; TFIIIB is subsequently recruited upstream of the transcription start site (TSS), and Pol III finally binds to the TSS through interacting with TFIIIB (Moir and Willis, 2013; Yeganeh and Hernandez, 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of type II transcription initiation, supported by citations.

claim: During type II transcription initiation of tRNA genes, TFIIIB is recruited upstream of the transcription start site after TFIIIC binding.
source: During the transcription initiation of tRNA genes (type II), TFIIIC initially binds to the internal elements box-A and box-B within the tRNA-coding region; TFIIIB is subsequently recruited upstream of the transcription start site (TSS), and Pol III finally binds to the TSS through interacting with TFIIIB (Moir and Willis, 2013; Yeganeh and Hernandez, 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of type II transcription initiation, supported by citations.

claim: During type II transcription initiation of tRNA genes, Pol III binds to the TSS through interacting with TFIIIB.
source: During the transcription initiation of tRNA genes (type II), TFIIIC initially binds to the internal elements box-A and box-B within the tRNA-coding region; TFIIIB is subsequently recruited upstream of the transcription start site (TSS), and Pol III finally binds to the TSS through interacting with TFIIIB (Moir and Willis, 2013; Yeganeh and Hernandez, 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of type II transcription initiation, supported by citations.

claim: c-MYC can modulate Pol III-mediated transcription.
source: In addition to Pol III general transcription factors, oncogenic factor (c-MYC), tumor suppressor (p53), and signaling transduction factors (JNK and PTEN/AKT) can also tightly modulate Pol III-mediated transcription (Gomez-Roman et al., 2003; Crighton et al., 2003; Sriskanthadevan-Pirahas et al., 2018; Zhong and Johnson, 2009; Woiwode et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: p53 can modulate Pol III-mediated transcription.
source: In addition to Pol III general transcription factors, oncogenic factor (c-MYC), tumor suppressor (p53), and signaling transduction factors (JNK and PTEN/AKT) can also tightly modulate Pol III-mediated transcription (Gomez-Roman et al., 2003; Crighton et al., 2003; Sriskanthadevan-Pirahas et al., 2018; Zhong and Johnson, 2009; Woiwode et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: JNK and PTEN/AKT signaling transduction factors can modulate Pol III-mediated transcription.
source: In addition to Pol III general transcription factors, oncogenic factor (c-MYC), tumor suppressor (p53), and signaling transduction factors (JNK and PTEN/AKT) can also tightly modulate Pol III-mediated transcription (Gomez-Roman et al., 2003; Crighton et al., 2003; Sriskanthadevan-Pirahas et al., 2018; Zhong and Johnson, 2009; Woiwode et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: MAF1 is a well-characterized factor repressing Pol III-directed transcription.
source: MAF1, a well-characterized factor repressing Pol III-directed transcription (Kulaberoglu et al., 2021; Bonhoure et al., 2020), has recently been shown to regulate osteoblast differentiation and bone mass formation (Phillips et al., 2022), and this factor has also been confirmed to improve cardiac hypertrophy and inhibit the synthesis of Pol III products by interacting with extracellullar signal-regulated kinase (ERK) (Sun et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: MAF1 regulates osteoblast differentiation and bone mass formation.
source: MAF1, a well-characterized factor repressing Pol III-directed transcription (Kulaberoglu et al., 2021; Bonhoure et al., 2020), has recently been shown to regulate osteoblast differentiation and bone mass formation (Phillips et al., 2022), and this factor has also been confirmed to improve cardiac hypertrophy and inhibit the synthesis of Pol III products by interacting with extracellullar signal-regulated kinase (ERK) (Sun et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: MAF1 improves cardiac hypertrophy and inhibits the synthesis of Pol III products by interacting with ERK.
source: MAF1, a well-characterized factor repressing Pol III-directed transcription (Kulaberoglu et al., 2021; Bonhoure et al., 2020), has recently been shown to regulate osteoblast differentiation and bone mass formation (Phillips et al., 2022), and this factor has also been confirmed to improve cardiac hypertrophy and inhibit the synthesis of Pol III products by interacting with extracellullar signal-regulated kinase (ERK) (Sun et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: tRNA biogenesis and specific tRNAs such as tRNALeu-CAA and tRNATyr-GTA are required for the regulation of senescence.
source: It has been reported that tRNA (tRNA) biogenesis and specific tRNAs such as tRNALeu-CAA and tRNATyr-GTA are required for the regulation of senescence Guillon et al., 2021.
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Pol III transcription and its products can regulate more biological functions than previously thought.
source: These findings suggest that Pol IIII transcription and its products can regulate more biological functions than we thought.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited findings about MAF1 and tRNA functions.

claim: Deregulation of Pol III products or the Pol III transcription machinery components closely correlates with carcinogenesis.
source: Deregulation of Pol III products or the Pol III transcription machinery components closely correlates with carcinogenesis (White, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Hepatocellular carcinomas induced by alcohol show abnormally high expression of BRF1 and Pol III products.
source: For instance, hepatocellular carcinomas induced by alcohol showed abnormally high expression of BRF1 and Pol III products (Lei et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: POLR3G silencing inhibits the expression of snaR-A, which is related to cancer proliferation and metastasis.
source: Pol III subunit G (POLR3G) silencing inhibits the expression of a small non-coding RNA (snaR-A) that is related to cancer proliferation and metastasis, and POLR3G upregulation is associated with poor survival outcomes in several cancers (Van Bortle et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: POLR3G upregulation is associated with poor survival outcomes in several cancers.
source: Pol III subunit G (POLR3G) silencing inhibits the expression of a small non-coding RNA (snaR-A) that is related to cancer proliferation and metastasis, and POLR3G upregulation is associated with poor survival outcomes in several cancers (Van Bortle et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: GATA4 drives Pol III-directed transcription and cancer cell proliferation by enhancing the expression of SP1.
source: In the latest work, GATA4 has been shown to drive Pol III-directed transcription and cancer cell proliferation by enhancing the expression of SP1, which can directly activate the transcription of Brf1 and Gtf3c2 genes by binding to their promoters (Peng et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: SP1 can directly activate the transcription of Brf1 and Gtf3c2 genes by binding to their promoters.
source: In the latest work, GATA4 has been shown to drive Pol III-directed transcription and cancer cell proliferation by enhancing the expression of SP1, which can directly activate the transcription of Brf1 and Gtf3c2 genes by binding to their promoters (Peng et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: STAT3 is an important effector in the IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling pathway.
source: Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3), an important effector in the IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling pathway, regulates diverse biological processes, including apoptosis, angiogenesis, immunosuppression, cell proliferation, and migration (Srivastava and DiGiovanni, 2016; Johnson et al., 2018; Lee et al., 2019; Yang et al., 2019b; Jin, 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: STAT3 regulates diverse biological processes, including apoptosis, angiogenesis, immunosuppression, cell proliferation, and migration.
source: Signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3), an important effector in the IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling pathway, regulates diverse biological processes, including apoptosis, angiogenesis, immunosuppression, cell proliferation, and migration (Srivastava and DiGiovanni, 2016; Johnson et al., 2018; Lee et al., 2019; Yang et al., 2019b; Jin, 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: During canonical STAT3 signaling activation, elevated IL-6 molecules bind to the IL-6-receptor α and form a complex with glycoprotein p130, which triggers the activation of JAK/STAT3 signaling.
source: During the activation of canonical STAT3 signaling, elevated IL-6 molecules bind to the IL-6-receptor α and form a complex with glycoprotein p130, which subsequently triggers the activation of JAK/STAT3 signaling (Srivastava and DiGiovanni, 2016; Lee et al., 2019; Jin, 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge about STAT3 signaling, supported by citations.

claim: STAT3 phosphorylation at tyrosine 705 (Y705) is mediated by JAKs, ABl, and c-Src kinases.
source: In addition to Janus-activate kinases (JAKS), STAT3 phosphorylation at tyrosine 705 (Y705) is also mediated by other kinases such as ABl and c-Src (Srivastava and DiGiovanni, 2016; Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Upon phosphorylation, STAT3 is dimerized and transported into nuclei through a nuclear localization sequence.
source: Upon phosphorylation, STAT3 is dimerized and transported into nuclei through a nuclear localization sequence, where phosphorylated STAT3 dimers modulate the expression of its target genes by binding to STAT3 consensus sequence (TTC[N]3GAA).
evidence: This is established knowledge about STAT3 signaling mechanism.

claim: Phosphorylated STAT3 dimers modulate the expression of target genes by binding to STAT3 consensus sequence (TTC[N]3GAA).
source: Upon phosphorylation, STAT3 is dimerized and transported into nuclei through a nuclear localization sequence, where phosphorylated STAT3 dimers modulate the expression of its target genes by binding to STAT3 consensus sequence (TTC[N]3GAA).
evidence: This is established knowledge about STAT3 transcriptional regulation.

claim: STAT3 regulates the transcription of genes related to survival (BCL-XL and Mcl1), cell cycle (CyclinD1), cell migration (MMP2, MMP9, and Vimentin), angiogenesis (VEGF, HGF, and HIF1α), and immunosurveillance (NF-kB and CXCL10).
source: STAT3 has been shown to regulate the transcription of genes related to survival (BCL-XL and Mcl1), cell cycle (CyclinD1), cell migration (MMP2, MMP9, and Vimentin), and angiogenesis (VEGF, HGF, and HIF1α) and immunosurveillance (NF-kB and CXCL10; Lee et al., 2019; Catlett-Falcone et al., 1999; Lin et al., 2011; Xu et al., 2005; Chen et al., 2015; Stumhofer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Non-canonical STAT3 signaling plays a role in maintaining mitochondrial functions.
source: Besides, non-canonical STAT3 signaling has been identified to play a role in maintaining mitochondrial functions, and unphosphorylated STAT3 (uSTAT3) can regulate the expression of Mras, Met, Cyclin B1, and E2f1 genes (Srivastava and DiGiovanni, 2016; Yang et al., 2005; Yang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Unphosphorylated STAT3 (uSTAT3) can regulate the expression of Mras, Met, Cyclin B1, and E2f1 genes.
source: Besides, non-canonical STAT3 signaling has been identified to play a role in maintaining mitochondrial functions, and unphosphorylated STAT3 (uSTAT3) can regulate the expression of Mras, Met, Cyclin B1, and E2f1 genes (Srivastava and DiGiovanni, 2016; Yang et al., 2005; Yang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: STAT3 has become an appealing drug target for anti-cancer therapy.
source: Due to the positive roles in cancer development, STAT3 has become an appealing drug target for anti-cancer therapy.
evidence: This is an inference based on STAT3's role in cancer development.

claim: The STAT3 inhibitor SD-36 can effectively degrade STAT3 protein and suppress the growth of a subset of acute myeloid leukemia by inducing cell arrest and apoptosis.
source: Recently, Wang lab found that the STAT3 inhibitor SD-36 can effectively degrade STAT3 protein and severely suppress the growth of a subset of acute myeloid leukemia by inducing cell arrest and apoptosis (Bai et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: STAT3 can positively regulate RNA polymerase I-dependent transcription by controlling RPA34 expression.
source: In our recent study, we found that STAT3 can positively regulate RNA polymerase I-dependent transcription by controlling RPA34 expression (manuscript accepted).
evidence: This is supported by data from a manuscript that has been accepted for publication.

claim: 5S rRNA is an important component of ribosomes.
source: Since 5S rRNA, an important component of ribosomes, was synthesized by RNA polymerase III, we hypothesized that STAT3 can also regulate Pol III-dependent transcription to coordinate cellular ribosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ribosome composition.

claim: 5S rRNA is synthesized by RNA polymerase III.
source: Since 5S rRNA, an important component of ribosomes, was synthesized by RNA polymerase III, we hypothesized that STAT3 can also regulate Pol III-dependent transcription to coordinate cellular ribosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about RNA polymerase III products.

claim: STAT3 silencing in HepG2 and HuH7 cells severely reduced the expression of Pol III products, including 5S rRNA, U6 snRNA, and 7SL RNA.
source: Interestingly, STAT3 silencing in HepG2 and HuH7 cells severely reduced the expression of Pol III products, including 5S rRNA, U6 snRNA, and 7 SL RNA (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: STAT3 silencing in 293T cells reduced the expression of Pol III products.
source: As expected, RT-qPCR results were consistent with those obtained in the assays with HepG2 or HuH-7 cells (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: STAT3 is essential to maintaining normal transcription directed by Pol III.
source: These results suggest that STAT3 is essential to maintaining normal transcription directed by Pol III and functions as a positive regulator in this process.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing STAT3 silencing reduces Pol III products.

claim: STAT3 overexpression stimulated the expression of Pol III products, including 5S rRNA, U6 snRNA, and 7SL RNA.
source: Analysis of Pol III products showed that STAT3 overexpression stimulated the expression of Pol III products, including 5S rRNA, U6 snRNA, and 7SL RNA expression (Figure 1H and J, Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1H, 1J, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: STAT3 silencing dampened the expression of tRNA genes.
source: Noticeably, STAT3 silencing dampened the expression of tRNA genes detected in the assay (Figure 1K and L, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1K, 1L, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: STAT3 overexpression enhanced the expression of tRNA genes.
source: In contrast, STAT3 overexpression enhanced the expression of the same tRNA genes (Figure 1M and N, Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1M, 1N, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: STAT3 can positively regulate Pol III-directed transcription in 293T and liver cancer cells.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that STAT3 can positively regulate Pol III-directed transcription in 293T and liver cancer cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the collective experimental data from multiple cell lines.

claim: Pol III product levels correlate closely with cell growth or cell proliferation activity.
source: It is well established that Pol III product levels correlate closely with cell growth or cell proliferation activity (Moir and Willis, 2013; Turowski and Tollervey, 2016; Leśniewska and Boguta, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: STAT3 silencing reduced the proliferative activity of HepG2 cells.
source: Interestingly, STAT3 silencing reduced the proliferative activity of HepG2 cells (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell counting and CCK-8 assay data shown in Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: STAT3 overexpression promoted HepG2 cell proliferation.
source: In contrast, STAT3 overexpression promoted HepG2 cell proliferation (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell counting and CCK-8 assay data shown in Figure 2C and 2D.

claim: STAT3 depletion blunted the rate of EdU-labeled cells.
source: As expected, STAT3 depletion blunted the rate of EdU-labeled cells (Figure 2E and F); whereas STAT3 upregulation enhanced the rate of EdU-labeled cells, indicating that STAT3 can promote the proliferative activity of liver cancer cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by EdU assay data shown in Figure 2E and 2F.

claim: STAT3 upregulation enhanced the rate of EdU-labeled cells.
source: As expected, STAT3 depletion blunted the rate of EdU-labeled cells (Figure 2E and F); whereas STAT3 upregulation enhanced the rate of EdU-labeled cells, indicating that STAT3 can promote the proliferative activity of liver cancer cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by EdU assay data shown in Figure 2G and 2H.

claim: STAT3 can promote the proliferative activity of liver cancer cells.
source: As expected, STAT3 depletion blunted the rate of EdU-labeled cells (Figure 2E and F); whereas STAT3 upregulation enhanced the rate of EdU-labeled cells, indicating that STAT3 can promote the proliferative activity of liver cancer cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the EdU assay data.

claim: The presence of ML-60218 reversed the activation of cell proliferation and Pol III-directed transcription induced by STAT3 overexpression.
source: Strikingly, the presence of ML-60218 reversed the activation of cell proliferation and Pol III-directed transcription induced by STAT3 overexpression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B), indicating that Pol III transcription activation contributed to the enhancement of cell proliferation induced by STAT3 overexpression, although the contribution of other factors cannot be excluded.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: Pol III transcription activation contributes to the enhancement of cell proliferation induced by STAT3 overexpression.
source: Strikingly, the presence of ML-60218 reversed the activation of cell proliferation and Pol III-directed transcription induced by STAT3 overexpression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B), indicating that Pol III transcription activation contributed to the enhancement of cell proliferation induced by STAT3 overexpression, although the contribution of other factors cannot be excluded.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ML-60218 inhibitor experiment data.

claim: STAT3 silencing inhibited the sizes of liver tumors during tumor formation in nude mice.
source: Analysis of tumor sizes showed that STAT3 silencing inhibited the sizes of liver tumors during tumor formation (Figure 2I).
evidence: This claim is supported by tumor volume measurements shown in Figure 2I.

claim: STAT3 silencing reduced the weights of tumors derived from HepG2 cells in nude mice.
source: Interestingly, STAT3 silencing reduced the weights of tumors compared to the weight of tumors derived from HepG2 control cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by tumor weight data shown in Figure 2J and 2K.

claim: Tumor tissues derived from STAT3-depleted HepG2 cells exhibited lower expression of STAT3 compared to those derived from HepG2 control cells.
source: Noticeably, tumor tissues derived from STAT3-depleted HepG2 cells exhibited lower expression of STAT3 compared to those derived from HepG2 control cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical staining data shown in Figure 2L.

claim: STAT3 silencing suppresses liver cancer cell growth in vivo.
source: These results indicate that STAT3 silencing suppresses liver cancer cell growth in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the tumor formation experiments in nude mice.

claim: STAT3 depletion reduced the number of colonies and the size of individual colonies in colony formation assays.
source: Colony formation assays showed that STAT3 depletion reduced the number of colonies and the size of individual colonies (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–C.

claim: STAT3 overexpression increased the number of colonies and the size of individual colonies in colony formation assays.
source: In contrast, STAT3 overexpression increased the number of colonies and the size of individual colonies significantly (Figure 2—figure supplement 3D–F), indicating that both cell survival and proliferative activity contribute to the alteration of cell growth induced by STAT3 silencing or overexpression.
evidence: This claim is supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3D–F.

claim: Both cell survival and proliferative activity contribute to the alteration of cell growth induced by STAT3 silencing or overexpression.
source: In contrast, STAT3 overexpression increased the number of colonies and the size of individual colonies significantly (Figure 2—figure supplement 3D–F), indicating that both cell survival and proliferative activity contribute to the alteration of cell growth induced by STAT3 silencing or overexpression.
evidence: This is an inference based on the colony formation assay data.

claim: STAT3 knockdown reduced the recruitment of TBP, BRF1, GTF3C2, GTF3C3, and POLR3A at several Pol III target loci, including DNA loci encoding 5S rRNA, 7SL RNA, and tRNA-Met.
source: The results of ChIP assays showed that STAT3 knockdown reduced the recruitment of TBP, BRF1, GTF3C2, GTF3C3, and POLR3A at several Pol III target loci, including DNA loci encoding 5S rRNA, 7SL RNA, and tRNA-Met (Figure 3A–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP assay data shown in Figure 3A–H.

claim: The occupancy of TBP, BRF2, and POLR3A was reduced at the U6 snRNA promoter after STAT3 depletion.
source: Interestingly, the occupancy of TBP, BRF2, and POLR3A was reduced at the U6 snRNA promoter after STAT3 depletion.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP assay data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: STAT3 does not bind to the DNA loci that encode 5S rRNA, U6 snRNA, 7SL RNA, and tRNA-Met.
source: Unexpectedly, STAT3 does not bind to the DNA loci that encode 5S rRNA, U6 snRNA, 7SL RNA, and tRNA-Met, but it binds to the promoter of STAT3 target gene BCL2 (Figure 3I), suggesting that STAT3 does not directly regulate Pol III-directed transcription.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP assay data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: STAT3 binds to the promoter of STAT3 target gene BCL2.
source: Unexpectedly, STAT3 does not bind to the DNA loci that encode 5S rRNA, U6 snRNA, 7SL RNA, and tRNA-Met, but it binds to the promoter of STAT3 target gene BCL2 (Figure 3I), suggesting that STAT3 does not directly regulate Pol III-directed transcription.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP assay data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: STAT3 does not directly regulate Pol III-directed transcription.
source: Unexpectedly, STAT3 does not bind to the DNA loci that encode 5S rRNA, U6 snRNA, 7SL RNA, and tRNA-Met, but it binds to the promoter of STAT3 target gene BCL2 (Figure 3I), suggesting that STAT3 does not directly regulate Pol III-directed transcription.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ChIP assay data showing STAT3 does not bind to Pol III target loci.

claim: STAT3 silencing did not affect the expression of Pol III transcription machinery components TBP, BRF1, GTF3C2, and GTF3C3 in HepG2 and 293T cells.
source: Western blot results showed that STAT3 silencing did not affect the expression of Pol III transcription machinery components in HepG2 and 293T cells (Figure 3J and K), suggesting that the occupancy changes of Pol III transcription machinery components at Pol III target loci are not caused by the expression of Pol III general transcription factor subunits tested in the assays.
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3J and 3K.

claim: The occupancy changes of Pol III transcription machinery components at Pol III target loci are not caused by the expression of Pol III general transcription factor subunits.
source: Western blot results showed that STAT3 silencing did not affect the expression of Pol III transcription machinery components in HepG2 and 293T cells (Figure 3J and K), suggesting that the occupancy changes of Pol III transcription machinery components at Pol III target loci are not caused by the expression of Pol III general transcription factor subunits tested in the assays.
evidence: This is an inference based on the western blot data showing no change in protein expression.

claim: STAT3 silencing caused expression upregulation of 356 genes and expression downregulation of 590 genes significantly.
source: Analysis of mRNA transcriptome showed that STAT3 silencing caused expression upregulation of 356 genes and expression downregulation of 590 genes significantly (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: STAT3 knockdown did not alter the mRNA expression of components of the Pol III transcription machinery significantly.
source: The results showed that STAT3 knockdown did not alter the mRNA expression of components of the Pol III transcription machinery significantly (Figure 4C), suggesting that STAT3 regulates Pol III-dependent transcription through alternative pathways.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: STAT3 regulates Pol III-dependent transcription through alternative pathways.

claim: TP73 plays a negative role in the regulation of Pol III-directed transcription and cell proliferation mediated by STAT3.
source: Cell proliferation assays revealed that TP73 knockdown also reversed the suppression of proliferative activity caused by STAT3 silencing (Figure 5G), indicating that TP73 plays a negative role in the regulation of Pol-III-directed transcription and cell proliferation mediated by STAT3.

claim: TP73 knockdown enhanced Pol III product levels.

claim: TP73 knockdown enhanced HepG2 cell proliferation activity.
source: Interestingly, TP73 knockdown enhanced Pol III product levels and HepG2 cell proliferation activity (Figure 5J–L), suggesting that TP73 inhibits Pol III-dependent transcription and cell proliferation.

claim: TP73 regulates the Pol III transcription machinery assembly at Pol III target loci via mechanisms other than affecting protein expression.
source: Unexpectedly, TP73 depletion did not affect the expression of Pol III transcription machinery components, including TBP, BRF1, BRF2, GTF3C2, and GTF3C3 (Figure 6I), indicating that TP73 regulates the Pol III transcription machinery assembly at Pol III target loci via other mechanisms.

claim: TP73 can interact with TBP, GTF3C2, and GTF3C3.

In reciprocal assays, TP73 was precipitated by TBP, GTF3C2, and GTF3C3 (Figure 6J–L). These results indicate that TP73 can interact with TBP, GTF3C2, and GTF3C3.
